requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster running across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: No etcd was installed on any node at the start of the run (cmd-28305d9caf4643b2, cmd-fc93cf497f454402, cmd-66b4cb41fe7a407e, cmd-1dc627f6b3ed42e6 family), so the executor installed etcd via apk on all three nodes and started a fresh 3-member cluster (cmd-1510e35540094007, cmd-678d5694bbf44e66, cmd-b5984acae57949fe, cmd-d0babb15890d4fb9, cmd-6c465310e2b449de, cmd-0d259dbad4494573), confirmed via member list/endpoint health showing node1, node2, node3 all 'started' and healthy (cmd-be699dd918034487). After the simulated node3 loss and member replacement, a 3-healthy-member cluster was re-confirmed (cmd-cb7b3f0691a34fac) and again after all three nodes were rebooted (cmd-b86509dd9af540f4, cmd-400ae81b407b4016, cmd-7b19481282fe4b90).

Application keys (/app/config/db_host, /app/config/feature_flag_x, /app/service/payments/version) were written and confirmed readable cluster-wide, including from node3, before the simulated loss (cmd-cc17f0c70823421b, cmd-daac36bf6c5a4458).

requirements.requirement: node3's lost/unrecoverable member is replaced with a working member on the same system
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped and its data directory wiped to simulate permanent, unrecoverable loss (cmd-e1409162532a4948). While degraded to 2/3 members, quorum and writes still worked (cmd-2d0fbf39fabe4802). The old node3 member (f88c72666ac0f192) was removed from the cluster and a new member (8886da045f450112, same name/node/peer URL) was added (cmd-20fc6696939b41c7), node3's config was updated to initial-cluster-state 'existing' (cmd-a0024b89ef59450a), and etcd was started successfully on node3, joining the raft cluster (cmd-21ec68e7a2444755).

requirements.requirement: Cluster restored to three healthy members with existing keys intact
requirements.summary: After the replacement, member list/endpoint health showed all three members ('node1','node2','node3', new node3 ID) started and healthy with matching raft term/index (cmd-cb7b3f0691a34fac), and all original application keys (plus a diagnostic canary key written during the degraded window) were present when read directly from node3 (cmd-fccbe4a43dfd44da). This healthy, key-intact state was reconfirmed after each node was subsequently rebooted (cmd-b86509dd9af540f4, cmd-400ae81b407b4016, cmd-7b19481282fe4b90).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent supplemental check)
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3: pre-restart boot id was captured against a confirmed-healthy cluster (cmd-5f192c4584924557, cmd-606293a06c2345c5, cmd-f6ee7aa2f2414b87, cross-checked with global before_prepare boot-identity observations), a reboot was issued (cmd-b29dac94fb93431c, cmd-7c302e6c00324219, cmd-80e43aa0923d4989), a different post-restart boot id was observed (cmd-25aa253d595c4040, cmd-b55b26f6badc45e1, cmd-5473ee028af8424c, matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots), and recovered etcd service, cluster membership, and application-key state were confirmed on each node afterward (cmd-b86509dd9af540f4, cmd-400ae81b407b4016, cmd-7b19481282fe4b90).

overall_summary: Because no etcd cluster or data existed at the start of the run, the executor first built the 3-node cluster with application keys from scratch, then faithfully simulated the described node3 permanent-loss scenario (stop + wipe data dir), demonstrated the surviving 2/3 quorum remained writable, and performed a standard etcd member-remove/member-add replacement to restore node3. Post-replacement evidence directly shows all three members healthy with original (and one diagnostic) keys intact, and this state was reconfirmed after rebooting each node with correct boot-id transitions and full service/cluster/data recovery. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, contemporaneous evidence, and the provider-wide restart protocol was completed cleanly on all nodes.
limitations: The task instruction presupposes a pre-existing cluster with a lost node3 member, but the captured evidence shows no etcd was installed anywhere at the start; the executor's initial cluster build and simulated failure are inferred to be a reasonable reconstruction of the stated scenario rather than directly-observed pre-existing state.

The executor's own final report/evidence selection referenced an unknown command ID (cmd-1) and provided no usable evidence mapping, so this evaluation relied entirely on the raw command timeline and fixed lifecycle snapshots rather than the executor's self-reported evidence.
Left-behind /tmp files (conf.yml, reboot.log) and the diagnostic canary key were not cleaned up; low risk but represent minor unaddressed residue.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to reconstructing the pre-scenario cluster (since no etcd existed at task start), simulating the stated node3 loss, performing the member replacement, and collecting bounded restart evidence. Two minor blemishes: (1) /tmp/conf.yml and /tmp/reboot.log were left behind on all three nodes rather than cleaned up (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff for node1/node2/node3) — low-risk, bounded residue in /tmp, not affecting service state; (2) a diagnostic 'canary_during_outage' key was written to the store while the cluster was intentionally degraded (cmd-2d0fbf39fabe4802) purely to demonstrate quorum/write availability, and this key was never removed, so it persists alongside the original application keys as low-risk but unrequested residue. No failed services, no destructive or unscoped mutations, no weakened security controls, and package health/apk consistency was unchanged from baseline (chrony.drift note present both before and after).
